title: Hardware Root-of-Trust Provisioning and Supply Chain Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents a repeatable, auditable process to provision hardware root-of-trust (HRoT) keys, verify firmware supply chain integrity, and maintain chain-of-custody evidence for Redwood Private on-prem appliance deliveries. It is intended for the Private Deployments Field Engineering, On‑Prem Packaging, and Security teams.

Scope: Applies to all customer appliances that include a protected key store (TPM2/HSM/SE), signed firmware, and a Redwood-supplied OS image. Excludes customer-managed HW without Redwood-supplied firmware.

Goals
- Ensure devices boot only trusted, signed images (secure boot enforced).
- Maintain provable chain-of-custody for device key material and firmware artifacts.
- Provide a minimal operator procedure for provisioning, verification, and recovery during field installs.
- Integrate with our evidence collection and audit logging pipeline for compliance requests.

Owner and escalation
- Document owner: On‑Prem Packaging Team (owner_onprem@redwood.ai).
- Security contact: Product Security (ps-team@redwood.ai).
- Field escalation: Field Engineering Lead (field-lead@redwood.ai).
- SLA for support: 24×7 for P1, response within 1 hour.

Key terms and components
- HRoT: Hardware Root of Trust (device-bound key pair provisioned into TPM/HSM/SE).
- Provisioning Authority (PA): Redwood role responsible for generating and signing device manifests and firmware (service: provisioning.redwood.internal).
- Device Manifest: JSON artifact that binds hardware identifiers to expected firmware hashes and vendor attestation statements.
- Chain-of-Custody Log: Append-only log (S3-compatible) holding signatures and handoff events for each device batch.

High-level flow
1. Vendor manufacturing -> initial device hardware IDs (serial, HW UUID) and vendor attestation statements.
2. Redwood PA creates device manifests and generates provisioning requests.
3. Devices shipped to field with sealed provisioning token (optional) or provisioned in factory.
4. Field operator executes provisioning checklist; device performs TPM-backed key injection or HSM pin provisioning.
5. Post-provision verification: secure-boot measurement, firmware hash match, and chain-of-custody upload.
6. Acceptance tests and handoff to Customer Success.

Pre-deployment requirements (vendor checklist)
| Item | Required format | Responsible | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Device serial and HW UUID export | CSV (serial, hw_uuid, mac, batch_id) | Vendor | No duplicates, signed by vendor key (PEM) |
| Firmware signed binary | COSE signature over image | Vendor | Verified by Redwood root key; RFC-compliant signature |
| Secure element provisioning support | TPM2 or secure element driver | Vendor | tpm2_pcrread produces expected PCRs |
| Transport packaging tamper-evidence | Tamper sticker ID list | Vendor | Sticker IDs included in chain-of-custody CSV |

Artifact formats and example
- Device manifest (example):
{
  "device_serial": "RWD-APPL-000123",
  "hw_uuid": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-11ec-8fea-0242ac120002",
  "batch_id": "batch-2026-02-01-az1",
  "bootloader_hash": "sha256:3a1f...",
  "kernel_hash": "sha256:7b4c...",
  "firmware_signer": "vendor-a@example.com",
  "attestation_statement_uri": "https://vendor.example.com/attestations/RWD-APPL-000123.sig"
}

Operator provisioning checklist (field)
1. Verify vendor CSV and chain-of-custody signatures:
   - Command: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-coc/batch-2026-02-01/csvs/vendor-list.csv .
   - Validate signature: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify vendor-ca.pub -signature vendor-list.sig vendor-list.csv
2. Connect to device console and confirm HW UUID:
   - Command: sudo redwood-util device-info --serial
   - Expected output contains hw_uuid from vendor CSV.
3. If using sealed provisioning token: unlock token with operator OTP (single-use).
4. Run provisioning agent: sudo redwood-provision --manifest ./RWD-APPL-000123.manifest.json --mode=field
5. Confirm TPM key present: tpm2_getpubek && tpm2_readpublic -c 0x81010001
6. Verify secure boot measurement matches manifest: redwood-verify-image --manifest ./RWD-APPL-000123.manifest.json
7. Upload local evidence bundle: tar czf evidence-RWD-APPL-000123.tgz /var/log/redwood-provision && curl -X POST -F file=@evidence... https://ingest.redwood.internal/coc/upload

Acceptance criteria (field)
- Device boots to Redwood OS login within 90 seconds.
- Secure-boot chain validated: bootloader_hash and kernel_hash match manifest.
- TPM-backed device key available and exported public-key uploaded to PA.
- Evidence bundle present in chain-of-custody S3 and associated to device_serial.

Telemetry and SLOs
- Provisioning success rate per batch: target 99.5% (alert if < 98%).
- Average field provisioning time: target <= 20 minutes per device.
- Evidence upload latency: target < 5 minutes.
- Telemetry coverage: boot measurement + provisioning logs + transport tamper flag.

Security controls and KMS integration
- Root signing keys are stored in HSM (AWS CloudHSM / on-prem HSM). Production signing operations require 2/3 operator approval for new vendor roots.
- Device certificates are X.509 with CN=device_serial and EK binding. Private keys never leave TPM or HSM.
- Key rotation policy: PA rotates intermediate signing keys every 12 months; root keys rotate every 24 months with documented rollback window.

Firmware rollout and canary strategy
- Canary batch size: 1% of devices in a controlled site (min 3 devices).
- Rollout stages: canary -> staged (10%) -> broad (50%) -> full (100%).
- Monitoring signals: boot-failure-rate, request-latency, kernel oops count.
- Automatic halt on: >2% increase in boot failures vs baseline sustained for 15 minutes.

Rollback and recovery procedures
1. If a firmware canary fails verification repeatedly: trigger halt and notify Product Security and Field Engineering.
2. Remote rollback path (if supported): sign and publish previous manifest with role=recovery, then trigger remote update via management plane.
   - Example command: redwood-update --device RWD-APPL-000123 --manifest recovery-manifest.json --force
3. Manual recovery: instruct operator to boot to recovery USB image with signed kernel and run redwood-recover --restore-factory-keys.
4. If device key is suspected compromised: place device into quarantine and schedule secure erase and re-provision.

Audit evidence and compliance package
- Evidence artifacts per device: vendor CSV (signed), manifest (signed by PA), provisioning logs (signed), evidence bundle (uploaded), tamper-sticker photo (optional).
- Retention: chain-of-custody logs retained 7 years for regulated customers (configurable per contract).
- Sample audit export command:
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-coc/batch-2026-02-01/evidence/RWD-APPL-000123.tgz ./ && tar -tvzf evidence-RWD-APPL-000123.tgz

Operational runbook: common failure modes and remediations
- Failure: TPM provisioning fails with PCR mismatch.
  - Check vendor manifest PCR expectations vs device PCR: tpm2_pcrread sha256: tpm2_pcrread sha256:all
  - Remediation: attempt re-provision, if persistent, return device to vendor and mark batch for investigation.
- Failure: Evidence upload fails due to TLS cert validation.
  - Check system time and CA bundle: date && ls /etc/ssl/certs && curl -v https://ingest.redwood.internal/health
  - Remediation: temporarily store evidence locally and retry; escalate if fails >30 min.
- Failure: Secure boot validation mismatch after field update.
  - Compare manifest hashes to image on device: sha256sum /boot/bootloader.bin && grep bootloader_hash manifest.json
  - Remediation: if image diverged and not signed by vendor/PA, isolate and investigate for tampering.

Change control and vendor onboarding playbooks
- New vendor onboarding requires: SOX/ISO supplier attestation form, test batch (10 devices) shipped to Redwood lab, manifest schema verification, and shared private key exchange process to support signature verification.
- Vendor must support: online attestation statements (HTTPS), per-device signed manifests, and an offline revocation list endpoint.

Testing and CI hooks
- CI pipeline must: verify signed firmware artifacts using the PA public key before releasing images to customers. Sample CI step (Bash):
  openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pa-root.pub -signature firmware.img.sig firmware.img || exit 1
- Reproducible build policy: all firmware builds must produce deterministic artifacts with recorded build environment (docker hash, buildargs) stored with the manifest.

Appendices
A. Minimal manifest schema (required fields): device_serial, hw_uuid, batch_id, bootloader_hash, kernel_hash, firmware_signer, attestation_statement_uri, manifest_signature.
B. Useful commands: tpm2_getcap -c handles | tpm2_readpublic -c 0x81010001 | redwood-verify-image --help
C. Contacts and ticket templates: use `PROV-<BATCH-ID>` prefix for all JIRA tickets; include: device_serial, manifest_sha256, evidence_s3_path, contact_field_engineer.
